title: ascendc-tiling-design
summary: Design tiling for a custom AscendC operator: normalize the shape first (axis-collapse or flatten), answer the fullload-vs-split question for UB, apply the universal four-element template (multi-core split, UB split, buffer plan, branch matrix), and route per operator class (reduction, broadcast, elementwise, matmul, conversion) using algorithm-selection and chip-generation tables (DAV_2201 vs DAV_3510). Use when writing or restructuring an AscendC operator's tiling logic, before running any performance tuning campaign.

applicability.scope: Design or restructure AscendC tiling for the covered reduction, broadcast and elementwise classes, plus the bounded mxfp8 fusion and small-channel transpose cases.
applicability.input_contract: Operator class and semantics, normalized shapes/axes, dtype, target chip generation, valid/aligned lengths and intermediate-buffer requirements.
applicability.produced_artifact: A multi-core split, UB chunk formula, buffer-size/total-usage plan and branch matrix with edge tests; these are design outputs, not benchmark results.
applicability.failure_modes: Budgeting only inputs omits intermediate UB storage; mixing valid and aligned lengths or copy units corrupts boundaries, and choosing unsupported generation-specific primitives invalidates the design.

recommendations: Normalize axes first, then decide full-load versus chunking from the entire live working set; derive tile size from buffer, axis, API and load-balance constraints.
Keep valid compute/copy lengths separate from aligned storage offsets and sizes, and complete dtype, tail/alignment and boundary branches before tuning.
Select primitives by the target generation and preserve class-specific coverage limits; re-evaluate sample constants and API semantics instead of treating formulas as tested performance evidence.
